A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MissTSM, with matching core formulations and retained results despite v2's changed title and expanded scope. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original forecasting, classification, ablation, and computational-cost results, including experiments on ETTh2, ETTm2, Weather, and PhysioNet.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical results and adds backbone integrations, lake and solar forecasting, clinical classification, and PSM experiments. Some comparison scores are explicitly attributed to prior work.

M1.justification: The core TFI embeddings, positional encodings, MFAA mechanism, and MAE training remain. V2 extends the procedure with projection back to the original input shape for integration with other backbones (Sections 3.3–3.4), and introduces an Anomaly Transformer-to-missing-mask pipeline for PSM forecasting (Appendix G.2). These are limited extensions around the retained mechanism.

E1.justification: V2 adds Solar-Energy forecasting, naturally incomplete FCR and Mendota lake forecasting, P19 sepsis prediction, P12 length-of-stay classification, and forecasting on PSM data containing anomalies. P12 uses a different target from the retained PhysioNet-2012 mortality task. Earlier forecasting and classification coverage remains.

E2.justification: V2 adds reported comparisons with GRU-D, Latent ODE, LOCF, and RobustTSF with Autoformer. Table 10 additionally compares against methods including SeFT, mTAND, Raindrop, and MTGNN, explicitly importing their baseline scores from cited work. The original regular forecasting models, imputation methods, and MAE ablations largely remain.

E3.justification: New protocols include lake forecasting with context length 21 and horizons 28/35/42, AUROC/AUPRC evaluation on P12/P19, and PSM scoring that excludes ground-truth anomalous targets. V2 also labels Table 20's retained entries as 70% masking, whereas v1 specifies 60% MCAR and 70% periodic masking. This changes the reported setting without establishing a rerun.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained embedding-size, joint TFI/MFAA, hyperparameter, frequency/phase, and computational analyses, v2 adds a fixed-TFI-weight ablation under 60–90% MCAR missingness (Appendix E.2), backbone portability tests, and noise/anomaly case studies (Appendix G). New prediction-versus-ground-truth visualizations provide additional qualitative evidence.

E5.justification: Both versions report means and standard deviations over five masked-data realizations. V2 continues this practice in additional results; it does not establish an increased run count or introduce a new uncertainty-estimation procedure, confidence interval, or significance test.

E6.justification: V1 Table 4's numerical entries reappear unchanged in v2 Table 20, and the PhysioNet F1 score of 57.84% is retained. V2 adds extensive results for new comparisons, datasets, integrations, and ablations. For example, Table 19 reports PSM horizon-720 MSE of 0.815 for Anomaly Transformer + MissTSM versus 0.958 for RobustTSF + Autoformer; this is a new experiment, not a version-to-version performance gain.

T1.justification: V2 changes the mask definition from 0 = missing to 1 = missing, aligning it with the unchanged additive negative-bias attention formula. This is a limited mathematical correction, although the subsequent nonzero-attention implication is not updated consistently. The positional-encoding equations are relocated from v1's appendix, and no new proof or theorem is introduced.

C1.justification: V1 centers its contribution on novel TFI/MFAA components within an imputation-free MAE framework. V2 makes a broader claim of a model-agnostic, plug-and-play layer and positions the comparative investigation itself as a contribution. Its abstract and conclusion emphasize benefits under substantial missingness and limited simple periodic structure.

C2.justification: V2 develops substantive interpretations linking missingness and seasonality to imputation effectiveness, discusses why specialized models struggle with long forecasting sequences, and acknowledges circumstances where simple LOCF performs well. Appendix G adds applicability distinctions concerning noise filtering and anomalies. The existing limitation that MFAA relies on subsequent layers for temporal dynamics is retained.

D1.justification: V2 adds separate adapter/backbone hyperparameters, specific imputation and specialized-model settings, lake preprocessing and training details, and clinical/PSM setup information. It also explains implementation provenance, including GRU-D reimplementation. Conversely, v1's explicit training-set standardization, normalized-MSE description, and model parameter counts are omitted; this does not establish that preprocessing changed.

R1.justification: V2 adds a substantial Related Works section organized around forecasting, imputation, and imputation-free IMTS methods. It develops relationships to mTAN, ContiFormer, Compatible Transformer, and robustness methods, and positions MissTSM between imputation pipelines and specialized architectures. The earlier Chronos, decoder-only foundation-model, and BERT references are removed.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, conclusion, and results narrative are extensively rewritten. The brief experiments section becomes separate setup and question-oriented results/discussion sections, while the appendices are substantially reorganized. Existing embedding explanations and positional encodings move into the main text; the title, terminology, and author list also change.

P2.justification: V2 replaces the single-column layout with two columns, adds a conceptual taxonomy figure, and redraws the architecture diagram. Existing figures are moved, resized, or combined, including the embedding schematic and PhysioNet comparison. Numerous new tables, bar charts, and prediction visualizations substantially change the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens evaluation on naturally incomplete forecasting data and against specialized IMTS alternatives, addressing important gaps in v1. The isolated TFI ablation, backbone integrations, and expanded implementation details make the method's usefulness and component contributions easier to assess. Ambiguous metric labeling in Table 12, the masking-label conflict in Table 20, and omitted normalization details weaken reporting clarity, but the broader and more targeted validation provides a substantial net quality improvement.
